The Polypodiidae , commonly called leptosporangiate ferns , formerly Leptosporangiatae , are one of four subclasses of ferns , the largest of these being the largest group of living ferns, including some 11,000 species worldwide. [ 4 ] [ 5 ] [ 6 ] The group has also been treated as the class Pteridopsida or Polypodiopsida, [ 7 ] although other classifications assign them a different rank. [ 8 ] Older names for the group include Filicidae and Filicales , although at least the "water ferns" (now the Salviniales ) were then treated separately.
